items.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: the music of Jimmy Lunceford and Duke Ellington opened a new world of possibilities for Ruth.

ctx.x: Ruth Lion has held a lifelong passion for jazz and its artists. Her mother was a classical musician but the music of Jimmy Lunceford and Duke Ellington opened a new world of possibilities for Ruth. She found work as a jazz DJ in New York City and put records from the Blue Note label high on her playlist.

Alfred Lion, founder of Blue Note, tracked this heavy airplay to its source and Ruth and Alfred were married shortly after. Blue Note became one of America’s most respected labels and launched the careers of an impressive list of jazz artists. After Blue Note was sold to Liberty Records in 1966, Alfred and Ruth moved to Mexico for ten years, later settling in Ranch Bernardo, California.
